name: Course Orientation
description: The first class of a term: what the course covers, the term plan, how grading works, an ice-breaker, expectations, and why the subject matters.
audience: First day of term, new batch orientation, course introductions.

signals.why: your words describe a first class or orientation

slides.guidance: Welcome to {topic}, with a subtitle naming the class and term.
What students will be able to do by the end of the course.
The term plan: units or months in order, with assessments marked.
How work is assessed and graded, in clear points.
A short ice-breaker connected to the subject: instructions, minutes, grouping.
Why this subject matters in life and careers.
Questions about what students hope to learn and what worries them.
What to bring, where to find material, how to reach the teacher.
